cim: The pathetic tyranny of artificial intelligence
cim_eredeti: The pathetic tyranny of artificial intelligence
szoveg_eredeti:
No one can fail to notice the ever-increasing claims of artificial intelligence’s impact on diverse aspects of our lives. Like Napoleonic France in Europe, it imperialistically colonizes every sphere of human existence and insists upon doing so. This is most firmly to be resisted.

A worthwhile human life has nothing to do with AI, and conscientious persons should want nothing to do with it. This is true even putting aside questions about the ethics of particular AI models and companies currently in existence, for AI is, itself, contrary to human flourishing. It hardly needs to be said that students can have barely any legitimate uses for AI. In terms of their own learning, AI serves only to interdict it, and students have superior resources available to them for anything else. However, the world — or at least those in power — continues to insist on this abominable imposition.

Those who claim that ignorance of AI will render one unemployable in the future, for all work shall depend on AI, have the most impoverished conception of man qua worker imaginable. Not that the present dynamic of total work — to borrow a phrase from 20th-century Catholic philosopher Josef Pieper — is the epitome of the human condition, but most workers nonetheless exercise an expression of their humanity: They have some skill which is not had by others that enables them to undertake their employment.

This kind of worker is almost a perversion of the concept of the artisan, though the emphasis is on his, in a sense, mechanical skill rather than mastery, yet this state is redeemable. By contrast, the worker whose work is dependent on the exercise of AI is rather transformed into a mindless superintendent of a machine which serves only to regurgitate the pre-exercised talents of others, and which cannot be honestly said to have any skill in and of itself. The worker who presides over this process is rather like a man taken from the street and forced into the role of circus master for animals which he has been told have certain talents, but with which he himself is wholly unfamiliar.

As for those who voluntarily engage with AI in this manner on the grounds that, by utilizing it as a tool — as they so often like to claim — they are able to produce things which they could not otherwise create, thus realizing a revolutionary vision which was already present in their mind and, but for a lack of resources, could be brought to fruition through ordinary means: Such persons commit a double offense. First, they insult those who do in fact possess the skills necessary to actualize such a vision by valuing them as something which can be outsourced to the mechanistic, unhuman circus of AI. Second, they commit a kind of sacrilege, seeking to make themselves like God, by whose Word all things were made. “Man said to ChatGPT: ‘Let there be light.’” Except this is, of course, impossible, and in truth man makes himself only a gnostic intelligence, utterly impotent to fashion anything by his own will and reduced to ordering a demiurge to create what he himself cannot. One who could do nothing without AI can do no more with it, except pretend that one could.

These so-called uses of AI are thus a trap. It is by now well established that at least certain overuses of AI reduce one’s ability to engage in serious thinking — an unsurprising conclusion, given the long history of brain-muscle analogies. Therefore, by employing artificial intelligence in any way which serves to replace any kind of skill, we reduce ourselves to a servile status, subjects of a nonbeing, which has no real existence in the way in which humans do: The person thus enslaved lives the lowest form of life, exercising not an iota of his humanity, and subservient to the most powerless force imaginable. Let us then, who are not yet in that pitiable state, call to mind the words of Boethius: “No compact is made between good and wicked.” (Consolation of Philosophy, IV.6.48).

prioritas.indok: Subjektív, szkeptikus véleménycikk a mesterséges intelligencia ellen, konkrét hírérték és tények nélkül.
prioritas.cim_hu: A mesterséges intelligencia szánalmas zsarnoksága ellen érvel egy új véleménycikk
prioritas.lead_hu: Egy elemző cikkben ellenérzéseit fejezi ki a mesterséges intelligencia életünk minden területére kiterjedő térnyerésével szemben. A szerző szerint a tudatos embereknek el kell utasítaniuk a technológiát.
